key_idea: Use axisymmetric Euler with very weakly vanishing (C^{1,α}) vorticity in α-scaled polar coordinates. There, the leading-order dynamics reduce to an explicitly solvable 'fundamental model' with self-similar blow-up profile z/(1+z)^2. The full problem is then treated as a small perturbation of that model, using weighted coercivity of the linearized operator.
reason: The reduction to an explicit fundamental model with exact self-similar solutions is a striking conceptual move that explains why blow-up occurs. However, the bulk of the proof is a long chain of weighted Hardy inequalities, elliptic estimates, product rules and nonlinear bounds with large explicit constants, so the core idea is buried under heavy technical bookkeeping.
recognized: Elgindi, 'Finite-time singularity formation for C^{1,α} solutions to the incompressible Euler equations on R^3'
